I found nothing to flag: every claim in the document is supported by the record, and the one went_wrong item is not something its field excludes.

- **Root cause and the code path:** these are given as Code-Fix's reading of the source (F1). The document marks that reading as unverified in the root cause and says "likely" in the plain-words cause and in causal_chain 4.
- **Flag evidence:** the logs show the flag read on every minute from 08:57 to 09:26 (G153f). In the change minute, 09:27, 20 of 200 evaluations read off (G7ad6). From 09:28 to 09:34 every evaluation read off (G7037). The 09:34 limit is where the logs read stop, so "every minute after it" holds for the stretch that was read.
- **Contributing factor 1, "within the minute":** I took this to mean within about 60 seconds of the 09:27:52 change, since all evaluations read off from 09:28. Only 20 of 200 had switched during 09:27 itself, so a stricter reading of "the minute" would not hold.
- **Nobody was paged:** the record names this as a finding of its own, so it belongs in went_wrong. "No person was brought in to respond" is not the "no person was told" the writer was asked to leave out.
- **Not judged:** the action items and the what-ifs ("had it been otherwise").

supported.quote: With legacy-checkout-fallback off, account pages take the monthly spend-summary path. There, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`, and nothing guards against that number being zero. So for any shopper who has bought before but not this month it raises ZeroDivisionError, which `render_spend_summary` passes up to `serve_account_page`, and the page is recorded as failed. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

An administrator switched off a feature setting, which sent account pages through a monthly spending summary that likely breaks, by dividing by zero, for any shopper who has bought before but nothing this month.
If legacy-checkout-fallback is switched off again, account pages can fail again for shoppers who have past purchases but none this month.
Account pages failed to load for many shoppers
Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the account page error rate rose far above its usual level.
The account page requests failed because rendering them raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. These errors first appear in the onset minute.
The division by zero began when admin switched the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off at {P1.1}.
Before that, every evaluation read the flag as on and account pages rendered normally.
Evaluations started reading off in the minute of the change and read off in every minute after it.
Another flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T15.2} flag change by anyone but Argus in the {T15.3} hour before {T15.4}, and that change was this one.

With the flag off, account pages likely take the monthly spend-summary path, which divides by the number of items bought this month, and that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.
The flag change reached all of io-shop's traffic within the minute it was made. No staged rollout and no check before the change was seen.

No test was seen that runs the account page with legacy-checkout-fallback off for a shopper who has past purchases but none this month. Code-Fix's new tests for that case raise against the current code.
The HighErrorRate rule waits {rule_waits} with its condition holding before it fires, so the error rate stayed high for some time before anything acted on it.
Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person was brought in to respond.
